note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official list as PlayStation publishes it. Every guide below is written for this entry, in our own words, and names its sources. Methods drawn only from the official description are labelled as our own advice from the description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum pops on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is nothing to do for it directly. Work through the roadmap stages in order — story, side strands, open-world cleanup, then money — and this one closes the list. It is the last trophy every player earns, by definition.
steps: Earn the other 54 trophies in any order.
The platinum unlocks automatically once the last one pops.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first story trophy almost every player earns. Just play the story from the start and finish the mission; it pops when the mission completes. Story missions cannot be replayed, but none of the story trophies can be missed — finishing the story earns them all.
steps: Start the story and play through the opening.
Complete the Gone Fishing mission.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 1 and this pops at the chapter's end. Before you leave Chapter 1, do the one thing on the whole list that might be missable: the first meditation for Positive Mental Attitude, offered at Jason's house after the Down to Earth mission — follow Lucia to the balcony and accept. Everything else in the chapter can wait until free roam.
steps: Play through all of Chapter 1's main missions.
Before the chapter ends, take the balcony meditation at Jason's house for Positive Mental Attitude.

The trophy pops at the chapter's end.

Keep a manual save at the start of each chapter: missions cannot be replayed, and a save per chapter is cheap insurance even though no story trophy can be missed.
steps: Play through all of Chapter 4's main missions.

That checklist is what the rest of the platinum is built on, so open it before starting cleanup.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The hardest trophy on the list and the real platinum gate. After the story, open Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion to see the checklist — progress made during the story already counts toward it. The list covers the robberies (gang operations, bank jobs, payday loan jobs and vaults), collectibles, shooting ranges, drone races, stunts and challenges, but it does not require everything: for example it asks for 300 of the 397 stunts and 15 of the 18 meditation spots. Work the checklist itself rather than guessing, and save this trophy for last before the platinum.
steps: Finish the story, then open Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion.
Clear the checklist item by item, using this guide's roadmap stages.
The trophy pops at 100%.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Any 250 of the 397 stunts in the game count, and the 100% checklist asks for 300, so keep going past this trophy if you want the platinum. Stunts are the jumps, airtime, near-misses and trick driving the game tracks as you play. The fastest route is to chase stunt jumps and ramps deliberately in free roam with a fast car or bike rather than waiting for them to happen by accident.
steps: Do stunts in free roam — jumps, airtime and trick driving all count.
Reach 250 completed stunts; keep going to 300 for the 100% checklist.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: There are 9 activity types in the game, and this pops once you have tried each one a single time — no wins needed, just one attempt at each. Work through the activity list during the story whenever you pass one: fishing, the shooting range, drone races, arcade games, bowling, meditation, races, hunting and the rest. If one type is still missing late on, check the in-game activities menu for the one you have never opened.
steps: Try one of each of the 9 activity types — one attempt each is enough.
The trophy pops when the last untried type is attempted.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold all 42 Shooting Range challenges across the 12 ranges. This is a skill trophy, not a grind: each challenge has a gold score threshold, so replay a challenge until you beat it rather than moving on with a silver. Use the range's own practice runs to learn the target patterns first, then go for gold with a steady aim — rushing the shots is what costs the medal.
steps: Visit each of the 12 shooting ranges.
Earn a gold medal in all 42 challenges, replaying any you miss.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win one Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 race locations. You only need one win per location, not every race at that location, so move on as soon as you win one. Drone races are about clean lines through the gates: cut corners where the course allows it, and restart a race the moment you crash badly instead of limping to the finish.
steps: Find a Top Fun drone race location.
Win one race at each of the 14 locations.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — each race only counts once, so you need 20 distinct events, not 20 wins in the same one. Work through the race types across the map: street races, off-road and any other series the game offers. Pick a fast, stable car for each surface and learn the route on a first run before pushing for the win.
steps: Enter races around Leonida.
Win 20 different race events, one win each.

steps: Find Cal and take his fishing challenge.
Out-fish him to win the challenge.

Play and complete one arcade game.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida — and this is the one trophy on the whole list that might be missable, so read this first. In Chapter 1, after the Down to Earth mission, talk to Lucia in the kitchen at Jason's house in the morning; she says she is going to meditate, follows to the balcony, and you choose Accept. That meditation is only offered in Chapter 1, and nobody has confirmed yet whether the trophy needs it, so do it before the chapter ends. The other spots are spread over 10 locations, and the last one needs Jason and Lucia playable together, which opens after Chapter 2. Note the safety net: the 100% checklist only asks for 15 of the 18 spots.
steps: In Chapter 1, after Down to Earth, meditate with Lucia on the balcony at Jason's house — do this before the chapter ends.
After Chapter 2, meditate at the remaining spots across Leonida's 10 locations.
Reach all 18 spots; the trophy pops at the last one.

Complete 50 challenges across the 8 groups.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build up a 4-star wanted level, then lose the cops and escape. The trick is the escape, not the stars: get the wanted level up with your partner in the car, then break line of sight and stay out of the search cones until the stars fade. Alleys, tunnels and fast cars help; the wanted level must clear while your partner is still with you.
steps: Get your partner in the car with you.
Reach a 4-star wanted level, then break line of sight and escape until it clears.

trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops in a row without losing your wanted level — the wanted level must stay on through all three robberies. Pick three shops close together, plan a fast route between them, and keep moving: linger and the cops will close in, but the trophy only asks that the wanted level never drops off. A fast getaway car parked outside the third shop makes the escape after it easy.
steps: Bring your partner and pick 3 shops close together.

Rare and unusual vehicles count the same as common ones, so variety matters more than value — hop into anything you have not driven before.

trophies.guide: Down 5 enemies during one single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the slow-time aiming mode, so set it up first: find a spot with at least 5 enemies grouped together, trigger Focus, and work through them quickly before it runs out. If you only get 4, the attempt does not count — reload a save or try a busier fight and go again.
steps: Find a fight with at least 5 enemies close together.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: The description is just 'choices made', and PlayStation tracks a count toward 500 for this one. In practice that means the small decisions the game keeps count of — dialogue choices, how you handle encounters, the branching calls you make as Jason and Lucia. There is no single trick to it: play the game making choices, and the counter climbs. It will usually finish itself over a full playthrough plus cleanup, so leave it ticking in the background and check the count in your progress menu.
steps: Make choices as you play — dialogue and encounter decisions all count.
Reach the tracked count of 500 choices.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: 'Second time's the charm' — this trophy is about succeeding on a second attempt at something you failed first. The honest note is that no published guide has yet pinned down exactly which second attempt it counts, so our own advice from the description is: when you fail an activity or a challenge, try it again right away rather than walking off, and the trophy should pop on the successful retry. If it does not pop on the first retry you try, keep it in mind for the next failed attempt.
steps: Fail an activity or challenge attempt.
Retry it right away and succeed on the second attempt.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: 'What the hell just happened?' — this is the game's strange-encounter trophy. Every GTA has its weird moments out in the wilds, and this one pops when you witness one: an odd event, an unexplained sighting, something that does not fit. Our own advice from the description, not yet checked in the game: explore the odd corners of the map — the swamps, the remote roads, the places with no reason to visit — at night, and the moment will find you. The cited guides are still mapping exactly where these events trigger.
steps: Explore Leonida's odd, remote corners, especially at night.
Witness the strange event when it triggers.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee attack from a moving vehicle — a melee drive-by. Get a vehicle moving, pull alongside a pedestrian, and swing a melee weapon as you pass. It is the bowling pun of the pair with Let's Go Bowling, but this one happens on the street, not in the alley. A slow drive-by in a quiet street gives you the best aim.
steps: Get a vehicle moving beside a pedestrian.
Hit them with a melee attack from the moving vehicle.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies, so this trophy feeds directly off the robbery grind for the 100% checklist — rob, then launder the bills through the contacts who take them instead of spending them dirty. Your contacts unlock as you progress, and each laundering run moves the total along. Save this for stage 4, when the robbery work is mostly done and the bills are piling up.
steps: Rob to collect Marked Bills.
Launder them through your contacts until $250,000 is cleaned.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Every shop purchase counts toward the total, so this one climbs on its own as you buy weapons, clothes, cars and upgrades through the game. If it is the last money trophy standing, the fastest way to close it is to buy the expensive things you actually want — vehicles and weapon upgrades — rather than wasting money on throwaway purchases.
steps: Buy things in shops across Leonida — weapons, clothes, vehicles.
Reach $100,000 total spent.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties around Leonida. Garages are the properties that store your vehicle collection, and they go on sale as you explore and progress. Buy each one as soon as you can afford it — they double as the storage you need for the vehicle collecting in Whip It Good and On the Spot. The total cost is steep, so do this in stage 3 or 4 when the robbery money is flowing.

Purchase all 8 garages.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Scooter Bros is the in-world delivery and vehicle app — open it, pick vehicles from your collection, and register them one by one. Any 10 vehicles count, so use the ones already sitting in your garages from the Little Boxes properties. This is a quick trophy once the app is unlocked and you own a few vehicles.
